A commit pushed after the pull request is marked ready starts a run in a different group. That run cannot cancel a draft-state run that is still in its lint job. The older run then reads `draft=false` at its Draft state step and runs the release and smoke jobs. Both runs can then run those expensive jobs, and the older one tests an obsolete commit. The documented rule that a new push cancels the previous run does not hold across this boundary. > > The overlap for a run that started as draft is documented as intended. The cancellation gap for the newer push is not. A fix needs a workflow design change, not a one-line edit, so no edit is proposed. > > > >
